Sam (CS): FYI - Nelora Health flagged a surprise EOM charge. Invoice has an extra 'Burst overage' line for $1,248 that the dashboard doesn't show. Dashboard tokens = 12,345,672; Invoice tokens = 15,123,954. Account: acct_00912. Need a quick triage before EOD so I can update the customer. :grimacing:
Nora (Eng): on it. Which invoice run/time was that? Did finance finalize PDFs at midnight UTC?
Sam (CS): It was the Feb invoice finalized 2026-02-28 23:59 UTC. Customer just sent the PDF and dashboard screenshots. They insist they didn't change traffic.
Matt (Billing): I can see an ingestion backfill job ran 2026-03-01 01:07 UTC that touched acct_00912. Could be late processing. BillingBot shows backfill job id 6789 completed after cutoff.
Olivia (Data): quick ad-hoc check — aggregating tokens by two timestamps (event_time vs processed_at) shows a delta. SQL I ran below (BigQuery syntax):
```sql
-- tokens by event time (what dashboard uses)
SELECT SUM(tokens) AS tokens_event_time
FROM `redwood-prod.ingest.tokens`
WHERE customer_account = 'acct_00912'
  AND event_time >= '2026-02-01' AND event_time < '2026-03-01';

-- tokens by processed time (what billing pipeline used for that run)
SELECT SUM(tokens) AS tokens_processed_time
FROM `redwood-prod.ingest.tokens`
WHERE customer_account = 'acct_00912'
  AND processed_at >= '2026-02-01' AND processed_at < '2026-03-01';
```
Olivia (Data): Results: tokens_event_time = 12,345,672; tokens_processed_time = 15,123,954. The extra ~2.78M tokens have event_time in Feb but were processed in Mar (processed_at >= 2026-03-01).
Nora (Eng): That matches the backfill timeline Matt mentioned. Dashboard uses event_time window; billing job that generated the invoice appears to have used processed_at for the month window. If processed_at was used by billing aggregation, late-processed Feb events that landed in Mar could have been included in the Feb invoice.
Matt (Billing): Confirming: older billing pipeline used processed_at for cutoff while dashboard aggs migrated to event_time. We have a migration note from last year but billing config wasn't updated for the backfill path.
Jess (Support): Customer is asking for remediation. Can we provisionally credit the overage while we investigate? They'll escalate if we don't respond quickly.
Matt (Billing): If it's our ingestion/backfill causing inclusion after cutoff, standard practice is to issue a one-off credit for the overbilled tokens and mark the account as waived for that adjustment. I can do that once we have an audit report with exact counts broken out by event_time bucket.
Sam (CS): Customer message: "We didn't run any bulk jobs. This is unexpected and will kill our budget." They want an ETA for a fix and whether we'll refund.
Olivia (Data): I exported the audit slices and put CSV in the shared drive: drive.redwood/exports/3160509876_acct00912_audit.csv. It has per-day tokens by event_time and processed_at, and the delta column. Sample rows:
- 2026-02-27: event_time=120,345 ; processed_at=1,242,305
- 2026-02-28: event_time=98,120 ; processed_at=1,123,010
(you can see big spikes on processed_at for late batches)
Nora (Eng): Repro steps for root cause verification (run in BigQuery):
```bash
# 1) verify late ingestion counts
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false '
  SELECT SUM(tokens) AS late_tokens
  FROM `redwood-prod.ingest.tokens`
  WHERE customer_account = "acct_00912"
    AND event_time >= "2026-02-01" AND event_time < "2026-03-01"
    AND processed_at >= "2026-03-01";'

# 2) compare billing window logic against invoice run snapshot
# (join invoice snapshot table to validate what the invoice aggregator used)
```
Nora (Eng): I can trace the billing aggregator for that run and confirm whether it used processed_at. If so, we'll need a patch to ensure the aggregator uses event_time for cutoffs or retroactively exclude late-processed events for month boundaries.
BillingBot: backfill-job-6789 completed: inserted 2,786,282 token events for acct_00912; started=2026-03-01T00:47:12Z finished=2026-03-01T01:07:04Z; source=ingest-retry
Jess (Support): I'll reply to the customer with: "We're investigating and will provisionally credit any confirmed overage caused by our ingestion backfill. We'll follow up with an audit report by EOD." Sam ok to send that?
Sam (CS): Sending now. Include the CSV link and note we may issue a credit.
Matt (Billing): I'll open a billing-adjust ticket and queue a provisional rollback/credit once Olivia's audit is attached. Ticket: BILL-2026-1543 (internal).
Olivia (Data): attaching the exact delta numbers in the CSV. Late tokens attributed to processed_at >= March 1 = 2,786,282 tokens => $1,248.10 using their plan tier pricing.
Nora (Eng): Next steps / owners: - Nora -> confirm aggregator cutoff logic and push patch if needed (ETA 72 hrs) - Olivia -> produce full audit file with row-level evidence (ETA 3 hrs) - Matt -> create billing adj and hold invoice reversal until audit attached (ETA 1 hr) - Jess/Sam -> customer comms and provisional credit note (ongoing)
Sam (CS): Thanks team. I'll update the customer that we found late-ingest backfill and that we're arranging a credit pending final audit.
Jess (Support): marking thread for finance review. :white_check_mark:
Sam (CS): :thumbsup:
